subject.title: Add external event hooks for quota and provider state changes

question: Should CodexBar own an opt-in core feature that executes user-configured local commands for quota and provider events under the proposed stable event and configuration contract?
rationale: The patch is technically credible, but repository policy requires explicit sign-off for new features with maintenance and privacy implications; code review cannot decide whether trusted local command execution belongs in CodexBar’s permanent product surface.

options.title: Sponsor core hooks
options.body: Accept the opt-in shell-free runner and stable event contract, with documentation that configured commands are fully trusted local code.

options.title: Narrow to event export
options.body: Avoid direct execution and expose events through a non-executing local output or IPC surface consumed by external tooling.

options.title: Decline the core surface
options.body: Keep CodexBar observation-only and leave automation to external tooling built around existing CLI or localhost data surfaces.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core hooks
recommendation.body: Accept the opt-in shell-free runner and stable event contract, with documentation that configured commands are fully trusted local code.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository owner approved the underlying quota-warning behavior and is the strongest available owner for this product and security-boundary choice.
